target_customer: Non-coders and makers who want a website or MVP from a text prompt
problem: Building a website requires design and coding skills; Makeasite generates and shares a live site from a prompt.
business_model: Consumer AI tool, monetization not found
product_category: Prompt-based AI website builder, later AI running coach app

founders.name: Neo Cho
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background given.

founders.name: Alex Reyes
founders.background_notes: Named as author of the Cadence YC launch post and as a maker and co-founder on the Product Hunt page; not on the YC company page.

competitors.name: Durable
competitors.what: AI site builder that creates a website in under a minute using GPT-3

technical_complexity.rationale: Prompt to site generation depended on third-party language models available by 2022, and a two-person team shipped an editor with sharing.

defensibility.rationale: Anyone with model API access could replicate prompt-to-site, and well-funded site builders were adding the same feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AI features were widely added by site builders; Makeasite's team later moved to a different product.

market_need_then: Interest in generative AI rose sharply in late 2022; no sourced evidence of paying demand for Makeasite specifically.

rebrands.why: Recent pivot to an AI running coach per the YC launch post; date not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launches in 2024 and a v2 in February 2025, per search results; no brand-level press found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that describes only the original product, and the team has moved to Cadence.

pivots.to: Cadence, an iOS AI running coach with real-time audio coaching
pivots.why: Not stated; the launch post calls Cadence a recent pivot and says the founders began it to improve their own health

outcome_analysis: Makeasite was a two-person S22 prompt-to-website tool in a category where Durable launched in October 2022 and larger site builders soon added AI. The team later pivoted to Cadence, an AI running coach, so the original product did not become the lasting business. No funding or traction is public, so whether the pivot works is unknown; the pivot_failed code is a weak inference from the pivot alone.
